footprintRule: Every override entry declares a footprint. A cut piece is rebound by PLATEID1 only when its representative point lies inside that entry's bufferedBbox; a piece outside it keeps the partition binding and is reported as a declined override. bufferedBbox is bbox expanded by bufferKilometres, the latitude span directly and the longitude span at the poleward edge, so it contains every point within bufferKilometres of the bbox. 500 km is twice the 250 km frame-conflict threshold: the override may reach one conflict distance beyond the plate's own present-day crust, which absorbs the difference between the Cao 2017 PLATEID1 assignment and the Cao 2024 partition outline, and no further.

rule.claimOrInference: inference: EarthHistory's own measurement, not a claim of Cao et al. (2017) or Cao et al. (2024)
rule.default: a cookie-cut piece rides the plate of the present-day Cao 2024 static partition that owns it
rule.measuredAt: interval mid-age, representative point of each piece, both rotation files loaded
rule.override: a piece whose source PLATEID1 appears in the class table below rides PLATEID1 instead of its partition owner, because the partition owner carries the class more than 250 km from where its own PLATEID1 would place it over most of that plate's area: the two are different reconstruction frames, not a small disagreement
rule.selection: audit-measured: conflictOver250KmPercent >= 40 and conflictAreaSquareKilometres >= 200000, summed over the 24 canonical intervals; the piece is still cut by the partitions, only its motion binding changes

shallowMarinePolicy: the sm table is large (27 plates, 26.3 % of sm area in conflict) because sm spreads over Pacific, Farallon and Marie Byrd ground that no continental PLATEID1 can pose; the plan's Phase 7 policy (emit only co-moving pieces, count the rest) is a runtime scope decision and is not applied by this compiler, which emits every piece with its frame-conflict flag set
